titleEvidence.exactExcerpt: Dairyland's Alma-Blair Transmission Project is part of a long-range transmission project that will improve reliability while delivering low-cost energy across the Upper Midwest.

route.description: Authorized South Route (PSC Final Decision). Segment 1A runs north from structure LQ-34-3 along the east side of State Road 35: 1.1 mi per the decision, 3,642 ft in the GIS. Segment 1B runs 0.5 mi east, triple-circuited with LN-10/LQ-18. Segment 2B follows the existing LQ-18 161 kV corridor east, double-circuited 345/161 kV, for 21.7 mi to the reconvergence point just NE of County Road A and State Road 93. Segment 5 continues 10.9 mi along LQ-18 to the existing Tremval Substation area. Segment 6 runs about 0.7 mi north, single-circuit, to the 345 kV switching station approved in 5-CE-158. The geometry is the PSC docket GIS centerline.
route.caveat: Not survey accurate. The geometry is the PSC of Wisconsin docket GIS (map service AlmaBlair_1515CE103) for the application's Proposed Southern Route, attributed 'Proposed Southern Alignment (3-28-2024)', plus the Segment 6 'Alternate End Point'. The PSC authorized this route 'as described in the application and data request responses and as modified by this Final Decision', and Order 10 allows minor post-approval adjustments. The decision gives Segment 1A as 1.1 mi, but the GIS segment is 3,642 ft (about 0.69 mi), so the western end may differ in the November 2025 revised application, which was not retrieved.

caveats: The route geometry is the PSC docket GIS centerline of the application's Proposed Southern Route (3-28-2024 alignment) plus the Segment 6 alternate end point. It is not survey accurate and may be adjusted after approval (see route.caveat). The Northern alternative was not authorized and is not traced.

The PSC Final Decision gives only a construction start (Q4 2026) and an in-service date (September 2028), not a construction end. Its start is recorded as a fact, not a construction window. The only windows with both ends come from the Dairyland page (2026-2027) and the outdated July 2024 application table (Q4 2026-Q1 2028).

The documented Xcel/NSPW interface is an interconnection at a shared switching station (Tremval North, NSPW-owned) plus interface design coordination described in the 2024 application. No source shows shared crews, equipment or other resource sharing.

The Tremval North point comes from the PSC's WWTC (5-CE-158) GIS layer for the candidate 'Tremval Expansion North' site, which the WWTC decision authorized. It marks the site, not a surveyed station footprint.
'not-found-in-sources' coordination entries mean the cached sources are silent. They do not mean the projects are uncoordinated.

unresolved: Application filing date conflict. The Dairyland page says 'In June 2024, Dairyland applied' and also 'CPCN application submitted in July 2024'. The cached application cover is dated July 2024, and the PSC decision notes that DATCP published the project's Agricultural Impact Statement on 2024-10-29. Yet the PSC decision records the application as filed 2025-02-14 and found complete 2025-03-17, with a revised version filed 2025-11-10. The cached sources do not explain the gap. The decision cites the application as PSC REF# 567118 ('page 21 of 270'), which does not match the 268-page July 2024 PDF; it is probably the November 2025 revised version, which was not retrieved.

Decision and service dates. The Final Decision is signed 'the 10th day of March, 2026'. PDF p.1 has an image stamp 'SERVICE DATE Mar 11, 2026' that is not in the text layer, so it was read visually and could not be verified by script. It matches the Dairyland page's 'Written Order was issued on March 11, 2026'. By Order 20 the decision would take effect 2026-03-12, so the one-year construction-start deadline in Orders 17-18 falls in roughly March 2027 or later, depending on permit and review dates.

Western endpoint line ID is inconsistent. Decision pp.1, 5 and 13 say 'existing LQ-43 transmission line'; decision p.14 says 'LQ-34-4 transmission structure'; decision p.28 and the application say structure 'LQ-34-3' on Dairyland's LQ-34 line. 'LQ-43' looks like a transposition but this is not confirmed. The PSC GIS start node is about 1.3 km south of the GIS Alma Substation point, while the decision says the start is 'just south' of the substation.
Decision p.13 spells the terminating station 'Tremval Nouth Substation' (typo), while pp.1 and 5 say 'Tremval North Substation'.

Decision segment labels are swapped. p.27 says the Southern Route's unique segment is 2B (Northern: 2A, 3, 4), but p.28 calls the Southern segment '2A' and the Northern one '2B'. The application and the PSC GIS both label the Southern unique segment 2B.

Length and segment differences. The PSC says the South Route is about 35 miles; the Dairyland page and the July 2024 application say 34 miles. Segment 1A is 1.1 miles in the decision but 0.7 mile in the July 2024 application and 3,642 ft in the PSC GIS. Our own arithmetic, not a sourced claim: the decision's segment figures (1.1+0.5+21.7+10.9+0.7) sum to 34.9 mi, while the 2024 application's 34 mi used a 0.7-mi Segment 1A and left out the 0.7-mi Segment 6 alternate end point.

Tremval North naming and position. The Alma-Blair decision calls it a 'new 345 kV Tremval North Substation'. The WWTC decision calls it a 'Tremval North Substation Expansion site', and its caption says 'Expanding the Tremval ... Substations'. The 2024 application describes an 'expansion location' about 0.5 mi northwest of existing Tremval on the north side of the Trempealeau River. The WWTC GIS point is about 0.9 km roughly due north of the existing Tremval Substation and about 0.36 km from the Alma-Blair GIS Segment 6 end node. The exact station footprint is not in the cached sources.

WWTC docket numbers differ: the July 2024 application cites 'PSCW Docket No. 4220-CE-188' (Xcel), while both PSC decisions use the joint NSPW/ATC docket 5-CE-158. The partner ids 'xcel-wwtc' and 'atc-nspw-grid-forward' used here are placeholders and must be matched to the ids the WWTC and Grid Forward clusters assign. WWTC's owners are NSPW and ATC; the Tremval North station is NSPW's.

The PSC decision does not state a construction end; it gives a start in Q4 2026 and in-service in September 2028. Its vegetation-clearing window ends 'by the start of the 2nd quarter (April 1st)' without a year (probably 2027, but not stated).

The July 2024 application's schedule is outdated and internally inconsistent. It assumed CPCN approval in Q3 2025, and its narrative start of Q2 2026 matches the Northern Route table 1.8-1 (ROW staking Q2 2026) rather than the Southern Route table 1.8-2 (ROW staking Q4 2026). Completion claims disagree: 2028 (Dairyland page), September 2028 (PSC), Q2 2028 (2024 application).

Route geometry: the PSC GIS alignment is attributed 'Proposed Southern Alignment (3-28-2024)'. The November 2025 revised application and any post-approval alignment adjustments (Order 10) were not retrieved, so the authorized centerline may differ in places, especially Segment 1A.

plan.md hypotheses. (1) Supported: the approved South Route ends at the switching station approved for the Western Wisconsin project, and Dairyland's page shows construction in 2026-2027. (2) Supported: the earlier application documents interface coordination only, not shared crews or equipment. (3) Only partly supported for Alma-Blair vs Grid Forward: this cluster's sources show only that Grid Forward (5-CE-157, ATC/NSPW) connects the 'Tremval-Arpin-Columbia Substations' and appears in benefit modeling. They do not say Grid Forward uses the Tremval North station, give Grid Forward's construction window, or document any Dairyland-ATC shared-resource plans. (4) plan.md assumed precise GIS might be unavailable, but official PSC docket GIS exists for the proposed Southern Route and was used.

Related Minnesota work under LRTP Project 4 is not modeled here: the Mankato-Mississippi River 345 kV project (MPUC E002/CN-22-532 and TL-23-157, filed 2024-04-02 by Xcel Energy, Dairyland, Rochester Public Utilities and SMMPA) and Dairyland's 13.3-mile 161 kV relocation in Wabasha County, Minnesota.

Dairyland page issues: the link text 'The Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity is available for viewing here' points to the July 2024 CPCN application PDF, not to a certificate; the 'Written Order' link is the final decision. The page also calls the regulator the 'Public Utilities Commission of Wisconsin'.
The PSC final decision copy used here is hosted on dairylandpower.com. It carries PSC REF#:582638 and PSC received and service stamps, but the ERF copy was not fetched to cross-check hashes.

Status 'approved' rests on the CPCN approval and the page's 'PLANNING' label. No cached source confirms whether on-site construction or vegetation clearing had begun by 2026-09-26; the PSC expected construction to start in Q4 2026.
Cost claims differ by version: $188,796,752 (PSC, authorized South Route, excluding AFUDC) versus $177,383,646 (July 2024 application, Southern Route).

The old trace used an unnamed OSM 161 kV line (way 258551045) as an inferred stand-in for LQ-18, plus magnetic-field table points and an undocumented Segment 5/6 junction at the substation center.
